entries.name: Claude Code
entries.what: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that runs in the terminal and edits, runs, and reviews code.

entries.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
entries.what: OpenAI's open-source coding agent that runs locally in the terminal (also ships as a desktop app).

entries.name: Cursor
entries.what: AI code editor with a built-in agent, plus the Cursor CLI for running the agent in the terminal.

entries.name: Gemini CLI
entries.what: Google's open-source terminal coding agent for Gemini models (deprecated for personal accounts in June 2026 in favor of Antigravity CLI).

entries.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
entries.what: GitHub Copilot's coding agent in the terminal, invoked as copilot.

entries.name: Aider
entries.what: AI pair programming in the terminal that edits code in your local git repo.

entries.name: Zed
entries.what: High-performance code editor with a built-in AI agent panel and support for external agents.

entries.name: Cline
entries.what: Autonomous coding agent available as a VS Code extension, CLI, and desktop app.

entries.name: OpenCode
entries.what: Open-source coding agent for the terminal, with a desktop app.

entries.name: Amp
entries.what: Sourcegraph's frontier coding agent available via CLI, web, and native apps.

entries.name: goose
entries.what: Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app and CLI) with MCP extensions, now under the Agentic AI Foundation.

entries.name: Kiro
entries.what: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE and terminal CLI.

entries.name: Continue
entries.what: Open-source AI coding assistant (VS Code/JetBrains extension and cn CLI); repo is now read-only after its final 2.0.0 release.

changes.before: You catch style and rule slips by hand in every PR
changes.after: Checks run on each PR and flag what breaks your team's rules

entries.name: Obsidian

changes.after: Decisions and specs sit in linked notes your agent can read

entries.name: Notion

changes.after: Your agent reads the spec page before it writes code

entries.name: Linear
entries.what: Issue tracking and project management app for software teams.

changes.after: Your agent picks up the issue and its context directly

entries.name: Raycast
entries.what: Extensible macOS launcher with commands, extensions, and AI.

entries.name: Warp
entries.what: Modern terminal with built-in AI agents.

entries.name: Visual Studio Code
entries.what: Microsoft's extensible code editor.

entries.name: Ghostty
entries.what: Fast, native, GPU-accelerated terminal emulator.

entries.name: Figma
entries.what: Collaborative interface design and prototyping tool.

changes.after: Your agent reads the real frames, spacing and tokens

entries.name: Linear MCP
entries.what: Lets agents find, create, and update Linear issues, projects, and comments.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http linear-server https://mcp.linear.app/mcp

changes.before: You paste ticket text into the agent and update status by hand
changes.after: Your agent reads the issue, works it, and updates status itself

entries.name: Notion MCP
entries.what: Lets agents search, read, and edit pages and databases in your Notion workspace.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http notion https://mcp.notion.com/mcp

changes.before: You copy spec text from Notion into every prompt
changes.after: Your agent searches and reads the right Notion pages itself

entries.name: GitHub MCP
entries.what: Lets agents work with GitHub repos, issues, pull requests, and Actions through GitHub's official server.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http github https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_GITHUB_PAT"

changes.after: Your agent reads PRs, comments and Actions runs in place

entries.name: Figma MCP
entries.what: Gives agents design context from Figma files and lets them generate code from or write to the canvas.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http figma https://mcp.figma.com/mcp

changes.after: Your agent builds from the actual Figma frames and variables

entries.name: Sentry MCP
entries.what: Lets agents query Sentry issues, errors, and traces to debug production problems.

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http sentry https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp

entries.what: Lets agents manage Supabase projects: run SQL, inspect schemas, deploy Edge Functions, and read logs.

install.command: claude mcp add --scope project --transport http supabase "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp"

changes.after: Your agent inspects tables and applies migrations directly

entries.name: Neon MCP
entries.what: Lets agents manage Neon Postgres projects, branches, and run queries and schema changes.

entries.name: Stripe MCP

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/

entries.name: Vercel MCP

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http vercel https://mcp.vercel.com

changes.before: You open the dashboard to find why a deploy failed
changes.after: Your agent reads deploy logs and fixes the build itself

entries.what: Gives agents web search, code search, and page fetching via Exa.

entries.name: Tavily MCP

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http tavily https://mcp.tavily.com/mcp

changes.before: You search the web and paste answers back to the agent
changes.after: Your agent runs live web searches and reads pages itself

entries.name: Cypress
entries.what: End-to-end and component testing for web apps that runs in a real browser

changes.before: You click through the app by hand after every AI change
changes.after: Your agent writes Cypress specs and reruns them on each change

entries.name: Storybook
entries.what: Workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation

changes.before: You check AI-built components only inside the full running app
changes.after: Each component gets stories you can view and test in isolation

entries.name: Grafana k6
entries.what: Load testing tool where you script traffic scenarios in JavaScript

changes.before: You find out the API falls over under load in production
changes.after: Your agent writes k6 scripts and you load test before shipping

entries.name: Bruno
entries.what: Open-source offline API client that stores collections as plain files in your repo

changes.before: You hand-craft curl calls to check each endpoint the AI built
changes.after: Your agent edits Bruno request files and runs them with the bru CLI

entries.name: CodeRabbit CLI
entries.what: AI code review in the terminal on your uncommitted changes, with agent-friendly output

changes.before: You read every AI diff line by line, alone
changes.after: CodeRabbit reviews local changes and your agent fixes its findings

entries.name: Greptile
entries.what: AI code reviewer for GitHub/GitLab PRs that understands your whole codebase, plus an MCP

changes.before: PRs wait for a human to catch cross-file bugs
changes.after: Greptile comments on each PR with codebase-aware findings

entries.name: Graphite CLI
entries.what: gt CLI for creating and syncing stacked pull requests, paired with Graphite AI review

changes.before: Your agent dumps a huge change into one hard-to-review PR
changes.after: Work lands as a stack of small PRs you review and merge in order

entries.name: PR-Agent
entries.what: Open-source AI PR reviewer that describes, reviews, and suggests fixes on pull requests

changes.before: You write PR descriptions and review AI code by hand
changes.after: PR-Agent auto-describes each PR and posts review comments

entries.name: DeepWiki MCP
entries.what: Remote MCP that answers questions about public GitHub repos using DeepWiki's generated docs

changes.before: You dig through unfamiliar library repos to see how they work
changes.after: Your agent asks DeepWiki about any public repo and gets cited answers

entries.name: Ref
entries.what: Docs search MCP that feeds your agent precise, token-efficient API and library documentation

changes.before: Your agent guesses at APIs from stale training data
changes.after: Your agent pulls just the relevant current docs before coding

entries.name: Microsoft Learn MCP
entries.what: Remote MCP giving agents search and fetch over official Microsoft and Azure docs

changes.before: Your agent hallucinates Azure and .NET API details
changes.after: Your agent checks official Microsoft docs and code samples first

entries.name: AWS Documentation MCP Server
entries.what: Local MCP from AWS Labs to search, read, and get recommendations from AWS docs

changes.before: You paste AWS doc pages into chat so the agent gets services right
changes.after: Your agent searches and reads current AWS docs itself

entries.name: Brave Search MCP
entries.what: Official Brave MCP server for web, news, image, video, and local search via Brave's API

changes.before: You search the web yourself and paste results to the agent
changes.after: Your agent runs Brave searches on its own while it plans

entries.name: Perplexity MCP
entries.what: Official Perplexity MCP for real-time web search, reasoning, and research via the Perplexity API

install.command: claude mcp add perplexity --env PERPLEXITY_API_KEY="your_key_here" -- npx -y @perplexity-ai/mcp-server

changes.before: You research libraries and errors in a separate browser tab
changes.after: Your agent gets cited, up-to-date answers from Perplexity mid-task

entries.name: Maestro
entries.what: Mobile and web UI testing with YAML flows, plus a built-in MCP server for agents

changes.before: You tap through the mobile app on a simulator after each change
changes.after: Your agent drives the app via Maestro MCP and saves flows as tests

entries.name: shadcn/ui MCP
entries.what: Lets your agent browse, search and install shadcn/ui and registry components

changes.before: Your agent guesses component APIs and hand-writes UI from memory
changes.after: It pulls real shadcn components from the registry and installs them correctly

entries.name: Storybook MCP addon
entries.what: Storybook addon that exposes your components and stories to agents over MCP

changes.before: Your agent invents new components instead of reusing your design system
changes.after: It reads your stories and reuses existing components with the right props

entries.name: 21st.dev Magic MCP
entries.what: Generates and fetches polished React UI components from the 21st.dev library via MCP

changes.before: You describe a UI and get a bland, generic first draft
changes.after: Your agent pulls polished, ready-made components you can drop in

entries.name: Railway MCP
entries.what: Railway's MCP server, now bundled in the Railway CLI, to deploy and manage services

changes.before: You click through the Railway dashboard to deploy and set env vars
changes.after: Your agent creates services, sets variables and deploys from chat

entries.name: Render MCP
entries.what: Hosted MCP server to manage Render services, databases, logs and metrics

changes.before: You dig through the Render dashboard for logs when a deploy breaks
changes.after: Your agent pulls logs and metrics and explains what failed

entries.name: Heroku MCP
entries.what: Lets agents manage Heroku apps, dynos, add-ons and Postgres through the Heroku CLI

changes.before: You juggle heroku CLI commands to scale, deploy and check logs
changes.after: Your agent runs deploys, scaling and log checks for you

entries.name: AWS CLI
entries.what: Official command line tool for managing every AWS service

changes.before: You click around the AWS console to inspect and change resources
changes.after: Your agent runs aws commands to inspect, deploy and fix infra

entries.name: Terraform MCP Server
entries.what: Gives agents live Terraform Registry provider and module docs, plus HCP Terraform workspace tools

install.command: claude mcp add terraform -s user -t stdio -- docker run -i --rm hashicorp/terraform-mcp-server

changes.before: Your agent writes Terraform with outdated or made-up provider arguments
changes.after: It looks up current provider docs and module inputs before writing HCL

entries.name: EAS CLI
entries.what: Expo's CLI for building, submitting and updating React Native apps on EAS

changes.before: You wrangle Xcode and Gradle builds and store uploads by hand
changes.after: Your agent runs eas build and eas submit to ship to the stores

entries.name: Prisma MCP
entries.what: Hosted MCP server to manage Prisma Postgres databases, compute apps and storage

install.command: claude mcp add --transport http prisma https://mcp.prisma.io/mcp

changes.before: You leave the editor to create databases and fetch connection strings
changes.after: Your agent provisions a Prisma Postgres database right from chat

entries.name: Drizzle Kit
entries.what: Drizzle ORM's CLI to generate, run and push SQL migrations from your TypeScript schema

changes.before: You hand-write SQL migrations and hope they match the schema
changes.after: Your agent edits the TS schema and runs drizzle-kit generate to sync

entries.name: MongoDB MCP Server
entries.what: Lets agents query and manage MongoDB databases and Atlas clusters

changes.before: You copy sample documents into chat so the agent knows your data
changes.after: Your agent inspects collections and runs queries against the real DB

entries.name: Redis MCP Server
entries.what: Official Redis MCP server for agents to read and write Redis data in natural language

changes.before: You poke at cache keys by hand in redis-cli to check behavior
changes.after: Your agent inspects keys and values to confirm the cache works

entries.name: PlanetScale CLI
entries.what: pscale CLI for PlanetScale databases, branches and deploy requests; MCP is now hosted

changes.before: You apply schema changes straight to production and pray
changes.after: Your agent opens a branch and deploy request so schema changes ship safely

entries.name: Upstash MCP
entries.what: Manage Upstash Redis databases, backups and usage stats from your agent

install.command: claude mcp add --scope user upstash -- npx -y @upstash/mcp-server@latest --email YOUR_EMAIL --api-key YOUR_API_KEY

changes.before: You open the Upstash console to create a Redis DB and copy creds
changes.after: Your agent creates the database and wires the credentials for you

entries.name: Convex MCP Server
entries.what: Lets agents introspect Convex tables, functions and logs and run queries

changes.before: Your agent guesses what's in your Convex tables and functions
changes.after: It reads your deployment's tables, functions and logs before coding

entries.name: Firebase MCP Server
entries.what: Firebase CLI's MCP server for Firestore, Auth, Hosting and other Firebase projects

changes.before: You flip between console tabs to check Firestore data and auth users
changes.after: Your agent reads Firestore, users and rules directly while it codes

entries.name: Snyk CLI
entries.what: Scans code, dependencies, containers and IaC for vulnerabilities; also runs as an MCP server

changes.before: AI-added packages and code ship without a vulnerability check
changes.after: Your agent runs Snyk scans and fixes flagged issues before you commit

entries.name: Socket CLI & MCP
entries.what: Checks npm/PyPI packages for malware, typosquats and supply-chain risk before you install them

changes.before: Your agent installs whatever package name it guesses
changes.after: Each package gets a supply-chain score and risky installs are blocked

entries.name: Trivy
entries.what: Open-source scanner for vulnerabilities, secrets and misconfigs in containers, repos and IaC

changes.before: Docker images and Terraform ship with unknown CVEs and misconfigs
changes.after: One trivy scan lists CVEs, secrets and misconfigs before you deploy

entries.name: TruffleHog
entries.what: Finds and verifies leaked secrets and API keys in git history, files and more

changes.before: An agent-pasted API key can sit in git history unnoticed
changes.after: TruffleHog flags live, verified secrets before you push

entries.name: OSV-Scanner
entries.what: Google's scanner that matches your lockfiles against the OSV.dev vulnerability database

changes.before: Dependencies your agent adds are never checked for known CVEs
changes.after: osv-scanner lists vulnerable packages from your lockfiles in seconds

entries.name: Wispr Flow
entries.what: System-wide voice dictation for Mac that turns speech into clean, formatted text in any app

changes.before: You type long prompts and specs to your agent by hand
changes.after: You speak the prompt and get clean text in the agent's input

entries.name: superwhisper
entries.what: Mac voice-to-text app with local and cloud models and custom AI rewrite modes

changes.before: Typing detailed prompts slows down how much context you give
changes.after: You dictate rich context and a mode tidies it into a prompt

entries.name: MacWhisper
entries.what: Mac app for on-device Whisper transcription of audio files and live dictation

changes.before: Meeting notes and voice memos stay locked in audio
changes.after: You transcribe them locally and paste the text into your agent

entries.name: VoiceInk
entries.what: Open-source, privacy-focused Mac voice-to-text app using local Whisper models

changes.before: You type every prompt to your agent by hand
changes.after: You dictate prompts offline and the text lands in your terminal

entries.name: LM Studio
entries.what: Desktop app and lms CLI to download and run local LLMs behind an OpenAI-compatible server

changes.before: Every model call goes to a paid cloud API
changes.after: You run open models locally and point tools at a local endpoint

entries.name: llm
entries.what: Simon Willison's CLI and Python library for prompting many LLMs, with plugins and SQLite logs

changes.before: Quick one-off model questions mean opening a chat app
changes.after: You pipe files into llm from the shell and every answer is logged

entries.name: Jan
entries.what: Open-source desktop app for chatting with local or cloud LLMs, with a local API server

changes.before: Your private code and prompts all go to a cloud model
changes.after: You chat with an offline model on your Mac via Jan's local API

entries.name: llama.cpp
entries.what: Fast C/C++ LLM inference engine with a CLI and an OpenAI-compatible llama-server

changes.before: Running a local model means heavy GUIs or cloud costs
changes.after: One command serves a GGUF model on a local OpenAI-style endpoint

entries.name: LiteLLM Proxy
entries.what: Open-source gateway that exposes 100+ LLM providers through one OpenAI-compatible API

changes.before: Each tool needs its own provider keys and has no spend limits
changes.after: All your tools hit one proxy with shared keys, budgets and logs

entries.name: Claude Code Router
entries.what: Routes Claude Code requests to other providers like OpenRouter, DeepSeek or Ollama per task

changes.before: Every Claude Code task, even trivial ones, uses the same model
changes.after: Background and simple tasks route to cheaper models automatically

entries.name: Datadog MCP Server
entries.what: Remote MCP server that lets agents query Datadog logs, metrics, traces, monitors and incidents.

changes.before: You copy errors and traces out of Datadog dashboards into the chat by hand
changes.after: Your agent pulls the relevant logs, traces and monitors itself while debugging

entries.name: Grafana MCP Server
entries.what: MCP server giving agents access to Grafana dashboards, datasources, Prometheus/Loki queries and alerts.

changes.before: You eyeball Grafana panels and paste metrics into the agent after a deploy
changes.after: Your agent queries dashboards, Prometheus and Loki directly to check the release

entries.name: CircleCI MCP Server
entries.what: CircleCI's hosted MCP server lets agents read build failures, logs and flaky tests and rerun pipelines.

changes.before: You open CircleCI, dig through failed job logs, and paste them into chat
changes.after: Your agent fetches the failing job logs itself and proposes the fix

entries.name: actionlint
entries.what: Static checker for GitHub Actions workflow files that catches syntax, expression and shellcheck errors.

changes.before: Agent-written workflow YAML fails only after you push and wait for CI
changes.after: actionlint flags broken workflow syntax locally before you push

entries.name: Lefthook
entries.what: Fast git hooks manager that runs linters and tests in parallel on commit or push.

changes.before: Agent commits slip through with lint errors and failing tests
changes.after: Hooks run lint and tests on every agent commit and block bad ones

entries.name: Husky
entries.what: Git hooks for JavaScript projects that run scripts like lint and tests before commits.

install.command: npm install --save-dev husky && npx husky init

changes.before: Agent commits land without anyone running lint or tests first
changes.after: A pre-commit hook runs your checks and rejects broken agent commits

entries.name: pre-commit
entries.what: Framework for managing multi-language pre-commit hooks from a shared config file.

changes.before: You catch formatting and lint issues in agent code by reading diffs
changes.after: Hooks auto-format and lint every commit before it is created

entries.name: JiraCLI
entries.what: Interactive command-line tool for searching, creating and moving Jira issues.

changes.before: You copy ticket details from the Jira web UI into the agent prompt
changes.after: Your agent reads and updates Jira tickets from the terminal itself

entries.name: Browser Use
entries.what: Python library and MCP server that lets AI agents control a real browser to complete web tasks.

changes.before: You click through the app yourself to check what the agent built
changes.after: The agent drives a browser through the flow and reports what broke

entries.name: Stagehand
entries.what: Browserbase's SDK for browser automation mixing code with natural-language act/extract/observe calls.

changes.before: Brittle selector-based browser scripts break whenever the UI shifts
changes.after: Plain-English steps like act('click login') survive UI changes

entries.name: agent-browser
entries.what: Fast Rust browser automation CLI built for AI agents, using element refs from page snapshots.

changes.before: You manually open the page to confirm the agent's UI change works
changes.after: The agent opens, clicks and screenshots the page itself via CLI

entries.name: iTerm2
entries.what: macOS terminal emulator with split panes, search, profiles and deep customization.

entries.name: tmux
entries.what: Terminal multiplexer for running many persistent shell sessions and panes in one window.

entries.name: Neovim
entries.what: Extensible Vim-based text editor with Lua config, LSP and a large plugin ecosystem.

entries.name: Knip
entries.what: Finds unused files, dependencies and exports in JavaScript and TypeScript projects.

changes.before: Agents leave behind dead files, unused exports and stray dependencies
changes.after: Knip lists the leftovers so you or the agent can delete them

entries.name: Oxlint
entries.what: Very fast Rust-based JavaScript and TypeScript linter from the Oxc project.

changes.before: Slow lint runs mean the agent skips checking its own JS/TS edits
changes.after: Oxlint runs in milliseconds so the agent lints after every edit

bundles.name: Project memory
bundles.why: You keep decisions in Obsidian notes your agent can read and write, plus a memory store it recalls each session. You stop re-explaining the project every morning.

bundles.name: Safe migrations
bundles.why: Your agent checks query plans before changing the schema, and every migration gets linted for locks and data loss before it ships.

bundles.name: Review relief
bundles.why: Reviewer agents and CodeRabbit flag bugs before you open the diff, and gh lets your agent read and answer PR comments. You review the flagged parts, not every line.

bundles.name: Browser testing
bundles.why: Your agent clicks through the app, reads console and network errors itself, and turns what it checked into tests that rerun on every change.

bundles.name: Ship with confidence
bundles.why: You run CI locally, catch leaked keys and risky code, and lint your workflows before you push. Fewer red builds and no secrets in history.

bundles.name: Talk to your agent
bundles.why: You speak long, detailed prompts in seconds instead of typing them, so your agent gets the full context. Pick one dictation app.

bundles.name: Cheap small tasks
bundles.why: You send renames, summaries and quick questions to a free local model and keep the frontier model for real work. Your bill drops without changing how you work.

bundles.name: Spec first
bundles.why: You write a spec and a task list before any code, and your agent works through it step by step. Fewer rewrites from vague prompts.

bundles.name: Fresh docs
bundles.why: Your agent reads current library docs, explains unfamiliar repos and searches the web before it writes code, so it stops inventing old APIs.

bundles.name: Design to code
bundles.why: Your agent builds from real Figma frames using real shadcn components, with a design skill that keeps it from looking generic.

bundles.name: Dependency guard
bundles.why: Packages your agent adds get checked for known vulnerabilities and supply-chain malware before they land in your lockfile.

bundles.name: Production debugging
bundles.why: Your agent pulls the real error, trace and user impact itself, with source maps so stack traces point at your code.
